answer: Mix planted answers into grading queues, like a wine judge served the same bottle twice. Each grader gets a few hidden plants: one plainly copied, one word salad that just strings juniper, yarrow and cedar together, one known solid. A grading farm that rubber-stamps every seat to collect pay scores the salad high, and its grading weight drops for later epochs. Evasion: actually read every seat, which makes each fake identity pay for real inference, the cost we want. Wrongly hit: honest graders with borderline taste, so only blatant plants count, and a miss cuts weight, never balance.
